facts.claim: Marriages and Divorces, Australia, 2025: 118,804 marriages were registered in 2025, 1.7% fewer than in 2024. The median age at marriage was 32.7 for males and 31.2 for females.
facts.source_name: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Marriages and Divorces, Australia, 2025
facts.use_note: REUSED from 2026-11-19 destination-cost research F-20 (checked date kept). Supports 'couples in their 30s'. No cost data in ABS.

facts.claim: Moneysmart's Marriage and money page gives no average wedding cost. It says: 'You can use our budget planner to help get a good overview of the money that will be coming in and going out.'

facts.claim: Foreign couples spent an average of €67,000 per wedding in Italy in 2025, a rise of almost 9% on the previous year.

facts.claim: The real wedding in Italy cost runs from about €20,000 to over €120,000, depending on region, season and guest count.

facts.claim: One Tuscan planner reports that a high-quality wedding generally lands between €800 and €1,200 per guest. On that basis, 50 guests sits around €40,000 to €60,000, and 100 guests around €80,000 to €120,000.

facts.use_note: REUSED from F-03. Supports the per-guest framing (guest count drives total). EUR. Nic sign-off.

facts.claim: Planners quote it in two main ways, a flat fee for a written scope or a percentage of your wedding budget, usually with a minimum fee underneath. Percentage fees commonly run at 10 to 15%, and some luxury planners charge 18 to 20%.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Cost of a Wedding Planner vs Planning It Yourself
facts.use_note: REUSED from F-18. Its AUD planner range comes from Airtasker (marketplace) and is not reused.

old_article_claims.claim: The Average (mean) cost of a Wedding in Australia is $67,307.37, and the Median Price (which is more reflective of what the average person spends) is $48,624.61.
old_article_claims.note: USER DECISION: no headline average. Do not use as a figure. The mean vs median point itself is a usable concept (mean above median shows skew), without the numbers.

old_article_claims.claim: Wendy El Khoury: Australian couples are increasingly spending their Wedding budget on creative ways to celebrate their union; supplier offerings in floristry, styling and design have evolved; social media plays a huge and vital role.
old_article_claims.note: Founder quote, nine years old. Re-quote only if Wendy re-confirms.

old_article_claims.claim: Running another survey; married in the last 2 years could win $500.

old_article_claims.claim: The average number of guests is 178; average bridal party 3.7 (4); average engagement 13.5 months; 22% used Uber or drove themselves; 30% of bridesmaids and 32% of groomsmen bought their own outfits.
'Average' means there are skews of data on opposite ends of spend. All Fairies have different budgets.
old_article_claims.note: Conceptual point matches the new angle (why averages mislead). Usable as a general statement, no figure. Page wrongly says 'medium' for median.

old_article_claims.claim: The average spend on wedding dresses is not reflective of what brides are spending: majority of spend in the 1-6k bracket, then upwards of 10k.
old_article_claims.note: Illustrates skew but figures are 2020. Use the idea only, not the numbers.

old_article_claims.claim: Coronavirus impact predictions: postponements into late 2020 and 2021, digital invitations rise, refined styling, demand for rescheduled dates, rise of local destination weddings and elopements, couples seeking payment plans for rings.
Surveyed over 500 brides who married in the last 18 months; overall 2019 median cost of a wedding $53,168, a 3.75% increase from last year; 6% increase 2017-2018 vs 3.5% 2018-2019.
old_article_claims.note: Do not use. Note internal inconsistency: 3.75% and 3.5% given for the same change.

old_article_claims.claim: Medians: honeymoon $10,145, engagement ring $11,753, entertainment $2,989; 23% did not go on a honeymoon; 33% of groomsmen and 31% of bridesmaids paid for their own outfits; average guests 162, up from 157; 36% took an uber/taxi or drove themselves.

Wendy El-Khoury: The spread is a lot broader, with more couples spending more and more spending less. This means the actual average is not indicative of what most couples are actually spending. Budget weddings sit at the 10-20k mark, luxury spend in excess of 100k.
old_article_claims.note: The principle (average not indicative) supports the new angle; the dollar bands are 2019. Re-confirm with Wendy before quoting.

old_article_claims.claim: Cakes and desserts, makeup and hair pricing has not shifted in 3 years; transport nearly doubled.
